liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like a Stranger** (1 review): First set includes the version from the With Out a Net album [35]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Described as MIDI sound at its best [28]
- **Dear Mr Fantasy** (1 review): Post-drums sequence into Hey Jude is noted as often overlooked [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-10-09.nak304.carpenter.89563.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 180 min; rated 4.8/5 by 10 [1]
- **gd1989-10-09.142510.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 24 songs; 184 min [2]
- **gd1989-10-09.mtx.dan.26236.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 179 min; rated 4.36/5 by 11 [6]
- **gd89-10-09.sbd.paino.2276.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 177 min; rated 4.62/5 by 8 [24]. Said about its sound: Fuller-sounding and cleaner than the other available source, though neither is crispy [34]
- **gd89-10-09.schoeps.howland.443.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 20 songs; 180 min; rated 3.79/5 by 14 [26]. Said about its sound: Quality is nowhere near the SBD recording but captures crowd energy [37]

## Around the show

- Rumored as soon as the band was announced to perform as the Warlocks [29]
- Biggest event in Dead land since Jerry returned from his coma [30]
- Crowd reaction to the first notes was electric and unbelievable [31]
- Crowd went wild and sustained roaring upon hearing the song's first notes [32]
- Crowd energy was deafening as the song broke out for the first time in years [33]
- Billed as Formerly The Warlocks after 1988 fan incidents banned the Dead [5]
- Lacks early 80s Jerry licks but offers qualities missing from earlier years [28]
- Considered one of the tightest shows of the Brent era [29]
- Ranked number one in Deadbase for the year 1989 [36]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-10-09.nak304.carpenter.89563.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Nakamichi CM300's w/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's, with no Dolby. Mics on stand on the floor, near the soundboard [1]. Also: ShnID-443 patches cover second set tape flips for Dark Star and Good Lovin [1]
- **gd1989-10-09.142510.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master (FOB)Audience Dat; Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics @ 110 degrees, ORTF, Schoeps t-bar stand, shoulder height > Monster… [2]
- **gd1989-10-09.mtx.dan.26236.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Dan Haugh; source: SBD + AUD Matrix Mix (60%-SBD/40%-AUD) [6]. Also: Sixty percent SBD and forty percent audience mix, aligned using Cool Edit Pro [6]
- **gd89-10-09.sbd.paino.2276.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> CASS(x)> DAT> CDR> EAC> SHN [24]
- **gd89-10-09.schoeps.howland.443.sbeok.shnf**: source: Schoeps CMC421 (note change from previous mic info)> DAT > SEK'D Prodif32 > SoundForge 4.5 (Level Increase & Resample - ) > CDWav>WAV > SHN [26]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1989-10-09 Hampton Coliseum, Hampton, VA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1989-10-09-hampton-coliseum-hampton-va-usa/) [41]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1989-10-09 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1989-10-09-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [42]

Rumored as soon as the band was announced to perform as the Warlocks
Considered one of the tightest shows of the Brent era
Biggest event in Dead land since Jerry returned from his coma
Post-drums sequence into Hey Jude is noted as often overlooked
Crowd reaction to the first notes was electric and unbelievable
Crowd went wild and sustained roaring upon hearing the song's first notes
Crowd energy was deafening as the song broke out for the first time in years
Fuller-sounding and cleaner than the other available source, though neither is crispy
First set includes the version from the With Out a Net album
Ranked number one in Deadbase for the year 1989
Quality is nowhere near the SBD recording but captures crowd energy
ShnID-443 patches cover second set tape flips for Dark Star and Good Lovin
Ted Mattes recorded master DAT; Charlie Miller handled transfer and coordination
Billed as Formerly The Warlocks after 1988 fan incidents banned the Dead
Sixty percent SBD and forty percent audience mix, aligned using Cool Edit Pro
